title: Ember: AWS EKS loyalty service, conversational with inline questions
proves: Questions asked inline without speaker labels, RTO/RPO in one sentence, time phrases in non-DR sections.
transcript:
Okay, let's get going. This is the handover for Ember, the loyalty points service. Shoppers earn and spend points through it at checkout, about two million transactions a day.

Ember runs on Amazon EKS in us-east-1. The points API is a Go service, and it stores balances in Aurora PostgreSQL. Redemption requests go through an SQS queue so checkout never waits on us, and ElastiCache Redis holds the balance cache.

So how do releases work? We merge to main, GitHub Actions builds the image, and Argo CD syncs it to the cluster. To roll back you revert the commit and Argo CD puts the old version back within a few minutes.

Monitoring is Datadog. The alert you will see most is queue age on the redemption queue, it pages when the oldest message is older than ten minutes.

What usually breaks? The partner airline API gets slow and the redemption queue backs up. When that happens, check the partner status page first, then scale the redemption workers to six replicas. The other one is the points API getting OOMKilled during the nightly expiry job, we raised its memory limit twice already.

Aurora takes automated snapshots, and they are copied to us-west-2. Our RTO is two hours and the RPO is fifteen minutes. We did a failover drill in March and it took ninety minutes.

Never run terraform apply from your laptop against prod, always go through the pipeline. And don't flush the Redis cache during the day, every balance lookup then hits Aurora at once.

Secrets are in AWS Secrets Manager and the pods get them through IRSA. Console access is through AWS SSO with MFA.

The busiest time is the week before Christmas, and there is a change freeze from the fifteenth of December.

We have dev, staging and prod accounts, and staging has a copy of prod data with emails scrambled.

The loyalty squad owns Ember. If it's down at night, page the on-call through PagerDuty, and escalate to Priya Nair, the engineering manager.

We pay for a three-year savings plan on the EKS nodes, and dev scales to zero at weekends.

One thing still open: the migration from the old SOAP partner API to the REST one is half done and nobody owns it after I leave.

In your first week get Datadog and AWS SSO access, and by the end of the month you should handle the on-call rotation alone.
